topics.label: Introduction to cancer biology and lecture learning outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic welcomes the students, frames the lecture series, and sets out what the lecture aims to teach.

topics.label: Accumulated genetic and epigenetic changes in cancer development
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the stepwise genetic, epigenetic, and infection-related changes associated with cancer development.

topics.label: Cancer as a failure of differentiation and tissue organization
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains cancer through the loss of normal differentiation and the disruption of organized tissue architecture.

topics.label: Cancer cell culture models and their limitations
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic describes how tumor cells are studied in culture and why isolated cells do not capture the full tumor context.

topics.label: Invasion, metastasis, and the distinction between benign and malignant tumors
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics use tissue invasion to distinguish benign from malignant tumors and show how invasive tumors can spread to distant sites.

topics.label: Benign tumors: progression to malignancy and clinical significance
topics.groupedBecause: Together, these subtopics explain why a benign lesion is not automatically malignant: some acquire invasive features over time, while benign growths can still matter clinically without doing so.

topics.label: Tumor nomenclature by tissue of origin and malignancy
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains how tumor names generally indicate their tissue of origin and whether they are benign or malignant.

topics.label: How cancer causes illness and death
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic describes how tumors impair normal bodily functions and how widespread metastases can lead to death.

topics.label: Tumor incidence patterns in humans and other animals
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics compare how frequently different tumors occur across human populations and animal species.

topics.label: Clinical presentation and cancer screening
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain why cancers can be difficult to detect early and compare screening approaches for different cancers.

topics.label: Lecture close: learning outcomes, revision and practicals
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic closes the lecture by returning to the learning outcomes and directing students to revision and practicals.
